name: Paranormal Shakti frontal session (to lower 'sensitivity')
summary: The frontal-lobe session of Murphy's retired Paranormal Shakti, which the vendor offered to adults troubled by reported paranormal experiences ('victims of paranormal pollution') to lower their 'sensitivity': 30 min of the hippocampal and amygdala signals one after the other, the same signal on four coils over the forehead.
setting: Adults (over 18) only (vendor). Investigators: not in the 3 days before an investigation, since the vendor says it lowers sensitivity.
schedule: Vendor: after 6 temporal sessions, 3 frontal sessions; 30 min each ('10 minutes will not be effective, and 40 minutes will be more than needed'). The vendor's general Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days.
notes: Coils: Fp1 and AF3 over the left frontal lobe, Fp2 and AF4 over the right; the exact sites are an inference from 'coils over the frontal lobes'. The other four channels stay unused. All four coils carry the same signal ('the same signal in both channels'), with no rotation. One 9.5-s pass: the hippocampal stand-in (five theta bursts at 5 Hz, each of 4 biphasic pulses at about 110 Hz, 0.84 s), 4 s of silence, the amygdala stand-in (the built-in accelerating burst, 6 to 30 Hz, 230 points of 3 ms = 0.69 s), then 4 s of silence; that gives about 9.6 s of field per minute, the vendor's figure for its standard signals. Both originals are proprietary; the hippocampal stand-in is the one used in the project's frontal reset session. The vendor reports headache or pressure in about 2% of users of an earlier version of its signals, mostly with hippocampal signals; if that happens, lower the intensity by one-third. The vendor excluded cases described as 'possession' (or took them only with caveats), and its wording came close to medical claims. This file makes none: it is not a treatment for anything, and anyone distressed by unusual experiences should talk to a doctor. Persinger's lab reported more acceptance of false statements after burst-firing over the left prefrontal region (Ross, Koren & Persinger 2008, single lab). Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). The product is retired; this file is of historical interest. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on distress.
